body:
**Nick Sleep and Qais Zakaria (Nomad Investment Partnership, 2001–2014)**
- **Core idea.** The idea began as "scale efficiencies shared" and was later renamed "scale economics shared." The firm passes the savings from scale to customers through lower prices. This drives volume, which brings more scale and still lower costs. Costco and Amazon are the canonical examples. — [Morningstar AU](https://www.morningstar.com.au/insights/personal-finance/254055/my-favourite-lessons-from-nick-sleeps-famous-investing-letters); [Chit Chat Stocks](https://chitchatstocks.substack.com/p/nick-sleep-how-the-secretive-investor)
- **Returns.** One source gives about 921% cumulative versus 116.9% for MSCI World (2001–2013). Another gives about 18.4%/yr. — [Chit Chat Stocks](https://chitchatstocks.substack.com/p/nick-sleep-how-the-secretive-investor). These figures differ by source; verify against the letters (the IGY Foundation PDF).
- **Other lessons.** Concentrate, distrust "massive over-diversification", and rely on patient capital. — [Rabi Chatterjee summary](https://rabichatterjee.substack.com/p/learnings-from-nomad-investment-partnership)

**Thomas Phelps (*100 to 1 in the Stock Market*, 1972) and Chris Mayer (*100 Baggers*, 2015)**
- **Phelps.** He studied 365 stocks that returned 100:1 between 1932 and 1971, and his advice was to "buy right and hold on." Commentary notes his work was more anecdotal than statistical. — [Hedge Fund Alpha, Mayer notes](https://hedgefundalpha.com/strategies/christopher-mayers-notes-100-baggers/); [MicroCap Club review](https://microcapclub.com/book-review-100-baggers-by-chris-mayer/)
- **Mayer's study.** He studied US 100-baggers from 1962 to 2014. — [Hedge Fund Alpha](https://hedgefundalpha.com/strategies/christopher-mayers-notes-100-baggers/)
- **Mayer's key idea, the "twin engines".** EPS growth combined with a rising P/E multiple. — [Validea](https://blog.validea.com/?p=33794)
- **Mayer's other traits.**
  - high ROE sustained over long periods
  - owner-operators and "intelligent fanatics"
  - a smaller starting size
  - a moat
  - a reasonable starting multiple
  - a "coffee can" holding discipline, after Robert Kirby: buy, put away and leave alone for about 10 years. Mayer calls it "a triumph of lethargy and sloth."
  - Sources: [Mindful Compounding](https://mindfulcompounding.substack.com/p/what-i-learned-from-chris-mayer); [Jimmy's Journal checklist](https://jimmysjournal.substack.com/p/how-to-spot-the-next-100-bagger-before)

body:
`insight:group-holdco-discount` · confidence: single-source

Listed holdcos in good groups (Bajaj Holdings, Tata Investment, Godrej Industries, Cholamandalam Financial Holdings, TVS Holdings, BF Investment/Kalyani Investment, and Grasim with its stakes in UltraTech and ABCL) usually trade well below the market value of their listed stakes. Commonly cited gaps are 40-70%, but that range was not re-derived here, so compute it yourself for each name. The reasons are structural: tax leakage on dividends and exits, no promoter intent to distribute or unwind, the holdco being used to fund new ventures (Grasim -> paints and B2B e-commerce), illiquidity, and control premia that accrue to the promoter, not to minorities. What actually closed gaps in this sample was a corporate event: a demerger or mirror listing (Bajaj 2008, Vedanta 2026, Piramal 2022), a regulator forcing a listing (RBI's upper-layer rule for Tata Sons, reiterated 17-Nov-2026, which matters for Tata Investment and SP group), a merger of holdco into opco (Piramal Enterprises into Piramal Finance, Sep-2025; GMR 2024), or a buyback/dividend policy change. Rules: (1) 'cheap vs NAV' is not a thesis without a named catalyst and its probability; (2) family disputes (TVS 2026, Kalyani 2023-26) can widen the discount; (3) holdco debt (Vedanta Resources, Bharti Telecom's planned stake build) changes everything, because the discount then reflects a claim ahead of minorities. Mark the 40-70% range unverified until computed.

Sources: <https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/tata-sons-listing-rbi-makes-its-stand-clear-again-asks-the-company-to-comply-567742-2026-11-17> · <https://www.angelone.in/news/market-updates/piramal-enterprises-shares-to-be-delisted-on-sep-23-shareholders-to-receive-1-1-allotment-in-piramal-finance> · <https://www.moneylife.in/article/vedanta-sets-1-may-2026-as-demerger-record-date-shareholders-to-receive-11-shares-in-four-new-entities/80266.html>

`insight:ind-as-accounting-levers` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-11-19 | tickers: GENSOL, INDUSINDBK

Checklist of where reported profit diverges from owner earnings (Buffett 1986) under Ind AS. (1) Revenue recognition (Ind AS 115): percentage-of-completion/over-time recognition in EPC, real estate, defence and software projects lets margins be front-loaded; watch contract assets/unbilled revenue and trade receivables growing faster than revenue, rising receivable days, and 'channel stuffing' near quarter-end (SEBI's Dec-2024 memo documents SME 'fraudulent sales and purchases through circular transactions amongst related parties'). (2) Capitalisation (Ind AS 16/23/38): capitalising interest, R&D/product development or 'pre-operative' costs flatters EBITDA and PAT; check CWIP ageing, capitalised borrowing costs vs finance cost, and intangible additions vs cash R&D. (3) Other income: treasury income, interest on loans to group entities, FX gains and fair-value gains (Ind AS 109) can be a large share of PBT; strip them out and ask whether core EBIT covers interest. (4) Exceptional items: recurring 'one-offs' (write-offs, restructuring, impairment) every year are operating costs; compare cumulative exceptionals over 5 years with cumulative PAT. (5) Related parties (Ind AS 24; SEBI LODR Reg 23 approvals for material RPTs): sales to/purchases from promoter entities, loans and guarantees to group firms, royalty to promoter-owned brands, and ICDs - Gensol (SEBI interim order 15 Apr 2025) diverted EV term loans to promoter uses; IndusInd Bank (Mar-Apr 2025) found internal derivative mis-accounting worth ~Rs1,960 crore cumulative P&L impact (Grant Thornton). (6) Off-balance-sheet: supplier finance/factoring and inventory sales to related SPVs (cf. First Brands, Marks Nov-2025). Test of truth: 5-yr cumulative CFO vs cumulative EBITDA/PAT, and cumulative FCF vs reported profits; auditor changes and qualified opinions are red flags.

| # | Stage | What broke | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | 3 | `fetch.py`: banks file only a **cover letter** on NSE ("transcript made available on the Bank's website"); it was flagged "scanned, needs OCR" and its letterhead became junk speaker turns ("Re", "Sub") | **Fixed:** cover-letter detector (whitespace-normalised, curly apostrophes), `skip` flag, turns.py skips them; new `--local PDF@DATE` in fetch.py/run.py adds website copies and replaces the cover letter |
| G2 | 3 | Quarter label: a 16-Oct call was labelled Q1 FY27 (20-day lag rule; banks report in 12–20 days) | **Fixed:** 7-day lag + quarter named in the transcript text wins (`common.quarter_from_text`) |
| G3 | 3 | **No bank measures**; "net interest margin 3.2%" was mapped to the finance-cost rule (false "missed") | **Fixed:** 20 bank measures (NIM, credit cost, GNPA/NNPA, slippage, PCR, C/I, CoD/CoF, yield, CASA, RoA/RoE, CET1/CRAR, CD ratio, loan/deposit/CASA/fee growth); bank rules run before the finance-cost rule; bps parsing; tight 5-bp tolerance for ratios; segment and multi-year-CAGR guards |
| G4 | 3 | **Pre-existing range bug:** "18–20%" / "3.2–3.3%" parsed as (−20, −20) because the dash was read as a minus sign; affected SKIPPER (9 targets, e.g. "20–25%" read as −25%) | **Fixed** in `parse_target`; SKIPPER statuses unchanged on 19-Nov data, but pending targets would have resolved as easy "delivered" |
| G5 | 3 | Chain logic compared floors, so a **raised ceiling on a lower-is-better metric** (C/I 53.5 → 55 → 56) was "same"; "3 years" → "at some point" was not a re-date; tolerance 0.5 pp too wide for bps metrics | **Fixed:** ceilings for lower-better measures, `deadline_dropped`, bank tolerances (2 bps / 25 bps) |
| G6 | 3 | Chain rule marked a **pending** original target "moved-goalpost" before its deadline | **Fixed:** stays pending with `goalpost_flag`; resolve at the original deadline (SKIPPER auto moved-goalposts 12 → 9; human statuses still win) |
| G7 | 3 | Data: screener bank page has no NIM/CASA/credit cost; `nse_fetch.py results` stops at Dec-2024 | **Fixed:** `nse_fetch.py integrated` + `bank_kpis.py` (XBRL: GNPA/NNPA %, CET1, RoA, NII, opex, provisions, diluted EPS; deck KPIs via `--manual`). Note: Q1/Q3 integrated filings carry **no balance sheet** for banks |
| G8 | 3 | Candour heuristic treated "slippages" as an admission word; categories had no bank labels (176 of 412 candidates = "other") | **Fixed** regex; bank categories added to the LLM prompt and `EXEC_CATS` |
| G9 | 3 | PEAD on reported EPS mixes treasury gains, provision buffers and one-offs; consolidated EPS also includes a 60.6%-owned NBFC | **Documented** (protocol v1.3): for lenders also compute SUE on PPOP-less-normal-credit-cost per share as a robustness check before acting on quintiles 1–2 |
| G10 | 3 | Credibility from conservative guidance looks excellent; MCS rewards sandbagging; card prints MCS as a % | **Documented/proposed:** add a "guidance bias" metric (actual − guide midpoint, in bps) and require a bank peer base (CUB, KVB, SIB, CSB, AU) before use |
| G11 | 3 | Management cites "guidance we gave" that is not in any earlier transcript | **Documented:** date promises from first traceable statement |
| G12 | 5 | Worksheet had no bank mode (revenue/EBIT/ROIIC meaningless for lenders) | **Fixed:** `tools/valuation/bank.py` (justified P/B, implied ROE, implied CoE, residual-income scenarios, RIM-consistent exit P/B, twin engine on book, P/B temperature, book stress, CoE×ROE grid), dilution for warrants; `worksheet.py --template --mode bank`; P/E examples unchanged (regression checked) |
| G13 | 6 | Decision card's stage-5 text assumed P/E-mode keys (crashed on bank results) | **Fixed:** `_bank_stage5_lines`; the four existing cards re-render identically except the version line. Remaining: §6 wording still says "exit P/E/DCF" (cosmetic) |
| G14 | 6 | No bank base-rate class (only an all-sector 2020–25 survivor class, bull-biased) | **Proposed:** stage-1 task: 5-yr outcome distribution of Nifty Bank/BSE Bankex members from several start dates, incl. Yes Bank, LVB, PMC-type failures |
| G15 | 2 | v2 hard rules are written for operating companies (fake cash, debtor days); lender checks lived only in `insight:lender-blowup-signals` | **Fixed in protocol v1.3:** a bank stage-2 checklist (divergence, AS-18 connected lending, frauds note, CET1/leverage, funding concentration, quarter-end vs average, ratings) |
| G16 | 2/4 | Basel III Pillar 3 and the bank website are behind a Radware bot wall; the Q2 FY26 transcript could not be fetched | **Documented:** use AR capital/LCR notes + XBRL CET1; fetch website PDFs manually (`--local`) |
| G17 | 4 | Protocol v1.2 had one line for lenders; no unit/cost/disclosure list for banks | **Fixed:** v1.3 bank/NBFC adaptation section |

title: FEDERALBNK_dryrun › 6. What broke (and what was fixed)

body:
- **Failure event (O_fail, India):** first of (i) IBBI CIRP admission of a listed-CIN company, (ii) IBBI liquidation
  order, (iii) NSE "Compulsory Delisting" or "Delisting - Liquidation", (iv) BSE delisted/suspended with no voluntary
  delisting or merger behind it. Date = IBBI announcement date (exact) or NSE delisting date; BSE-only events
  need a date from the last traded day (bhavcopy archives) - still to build.
- **Admission is not death.** Section 12A withdrawals, settlements with an operational creditor and orders set aside on
  appeal are common: Inox Wind (Jul-2017) and VA Tech Wabag (Sep-2017) appear as CIRP admissions on operational-creditor
  petitions and survived. Require, as in the US test, a price drawdown confirmation (for example >= 80% from the
  snapshot price within 5 years) or a liquidation / delisting event, and report admission-only cases separately.
- **Universe at each snapshot:** listed companies at T (BSE Active + Delisted + Suspended with ISIN, filtered by
  listing date) - this gets around the survivorship bias of today's NSE list. Financials at T must come from a
  filing made before T: screener keeps pages for many delisted firms (test next), else BSE XBRL results.
- **Name matching** is the weak link (renamed companies). Improve with BSE's former-name history or MCA CIN master
  data (MCA's site needs a CAPTCHA). CIN -> ISIN has no free bulk source that we found.

Screener still serves 87% of dead Indian companies (prices + annual tables) → survivorship-free Indian tests are
feasible now. Weighted 5-year failure base rate 19.7% in India vs 9.5% US. S1/S5-India ≈2× lift but CIs wide;
interest cover <1.5x is a genuine signal in India (2.87× for liquidation/compulsory exit). Dead banks with unlabeled
pages leaked past the financial filter (fixed in the test; live screen has the same small gap).
**Rule:** asymmetric costs justify keeping cheap "look harder" flags on consistent-but-unproven evidence; never
promote them to hard rules without proof.
